title: SqlBuilder.MakePerParentPagingOuter parameter-mode mirror (SqlBuilder.cs:822-835)
root_cause: key-divergence (pre-existing split-loader child plan key), NOT cache suppression and NOT HasUnkeyedScalarInValues
summary: The per-parent child command is rebuilt on every execution with a fresh Expression.Constant(List<TKey>) key-chunk predicate (EntityBuilderEagerLoading.BuildPredicate, EntityBuilderEagerLoading.cs:431-434). ExpressionPlanEqualityComparer.CompareConstant (ExpressionPlanEqualityComparer.cs:362-368) compares constant values with Equals, which for two distinct List<TKey> instances is reference equality. The freshly prepared child command therefore never produces a plan key equal to the stored one and is a plan cache MISS on every execution. Because the child command never cache-hits, QueryPlanner.RefreshParameters -> ExtractParams (QueryPlanner.cs:790-799) never runs for it, so the ParamMode pass never reaches MakePerParentPagingSelect/MakePerParentPagingOuter, and its parameter-mode mirror (SqlBuilder.cs:822-835) is unreachable through the eager loader. PerParentPaging/PerParentPartition are internal, so no public path can reuse a per-parent child command to trigger a cache-hit refresh.

options_ruled_out.cache-suppression: Ruled out: the miss is logged by QueryPlanner.cs:625-626 only when storeInCache && queryCommand.Cache, so storeInCache was true.
options_ruled_out.HasUnkeyedScalarInValues: Ruled out: that flag sets storeInCache=false (QueryPlanner.cs:584) and would silence the miss log; the log fired instead.
options_ruled_out.genuinely-unreachable-by-construction: Ruled out: the parameter mirror is reachable in principle from a cache hit; it is the fresh-constant predicate that prevents the hit.

probe_evidence.command: dotnet run --project tests/nextorm.sqlite.tests -c Debug -- -noColor -method NextORM.Sqlite.Tests.ScratchCacheProbe.Probe (TOTAL STATEMENTS variant)
probe_evidence.observation: TOTAL STATEMENTS=4 over 2 runs: run1 parent+child, run2 parent+child; the parent statement is reused while the child statement is re-rendered.

run1: Preparing parent > miss 1064916916 > Making sql param mode False (parent) > Preparing child > miss -537947611 > Making sql param mode False (child); run2: Preparing parent > plan cache HIT > Preparing child > miss 1982198788 (DIFFERENT hash) > Making sql param mode False (child).

probe_evidence.command: capturing ILoggerFactory, paged vs unpaged child, 2 runs each
probe_evidence.observation: paged child miss -665948566 then miss 1417499762; unpaged child miss 383837502 then miss 817739875; parent identical (-836302661). The child key divergence is present for both paged and unpaged children -> pre-existing split-loader behavior, orthogonal to D211 per-parent paging.

disposition: No Feature=D211 test can cover SqlBuilder.cs:822-835 through the public API; no production change (matches 'production-code edits only for a confirmed defect'). The pre-existing child plan-key divergence is a cache-miss (performance) characteristic, not a correctness defect, and is outside D211 scope; recorded as a non-blocking candidate observation, not a DO->PLAN blocker.
